compiled_state.title: As an engineer, Anthropic prompt caching with prefix-bytes invariant and cache-hit assertion bounds per-turn token cost
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Description

**What**: Place Anthropic `cache_control` breakpoints on the stable prefix (after system prompt; after diff), derived from rendered message structure not hardcoded by index. Add prefix-bytes-hash invariant test asserting the cached prefix is byte-identical across turns within a run. Add cache-hit assertion that warns on the first Anthropic call when both `cache_creation_input_tokens > 0` AND `cache_read_input_tokens > 0` fail to occur (tolerating CI-retry cache-warm state where read>0 is legitimate).

**Why**: SC3. Without caching, per-turn token cost across 15+ turns is prohibitive. Without prefix invariant, silent dynamic-content drift causes 5-10× cost overruns that look fine to the assertion.

**Scope**:
- IN: cache_control placement derived from rendered message structure; prefix-bytes-hash invariant test across turns; cache-hit assertion tolerating cache-warm; OpenAI prefix caching is automatic (no code change beyond placement)
- OUT: cache-cliff mitigation when c6de SC6 fallback fires mid-run (deferred to integration time, tracked in cross-epic interactions)

## Done Definitions

- When complete, every Anthropic call has cache_control placed at the system-prompt and diff boundaries, derived from the rendered message structure ← Satisfies: SC3 (placement)
- When complete, prefix-bytes-hash invariant test fails CI when any per-turn dynamic content (timestamps, turn counter, agent_id interpolation, randomized tip ordering, trailing whitespace) drifts the cached prefix between turns ← Satisfies: SC3 (invariant)
- When complete, cache-hit assertion warns to CI logs on the first call when neither cache_creation nor cache_read shows tokens, AND on subsequent turns when cache_read does not increase ← Satisfies: SC3 (operational visibility, CI-retry tolerance)
- When complete, unit tests written and passing for cache_control placement under all four (tier × tools-present) combinations and integration test asserting cache-creation on turn 1 and cache-read on turn 2 ← Satisfies: SC6 (caching tests)

## Considerations

- [Reliability] Cross-provider switch (c6de SC6) wastes the cache; mitigation deferred but documented
- [Performance] Cache invalidation from agent-specific prompt injection between system and diff is the highest-likelihood drift source — placement derivation must inspect actual message list at call time

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
